claude.sample_unit: patients (34,987 All of Us development cohort; 10,693 BioMe external validation)

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of stroke model in external cohort versus development cohort
links.effect: AUROC 0.745 in BioMe, but predictions systematically high (aggregate O/E 0.12 vs 1.00 in AoU), consistent with intercept-shift miscalibration.
links.quote: A machine-learning ensemble combining clinical, laboratory, and polygenic features outperformed traditional risk scores by 0.16–0.18 AUROC and retained discriminative validity in an ancestrally distinct external cohort but required site-specific recalibration of absolute risk.

links.outcome: Calibration after local intercept recalibration by ancestry group
links.effect: BioMe-fit intercept recalibration restored calibration in African American and Hispanic participants but not European American participants.
links.quote: Bio  Me -fit intercept recalibration restored calibration in African American and Hispanic but not European American participants.

links.outcome: Incremental discrimination gain from adding self-reported race as model input
links.effect: Race added small gains only with PRS (BioMe +0.022, P=0.034; AoU +0.006, P=0.052), not without PRS; overlapped with polygenic signal.
links.quote: The marginal contribution of self-reported race overlapped with polygenic signal, supporting per-ancestry calibration over universal race-aware model deployment.

unlisted_practices: Comparing ML model against established risk scores (rFSRP, PCE) on same data
Race-blind versus race-aware model specification comparison

models_evaluated: XGBoost M2 clinical plus laboratory feature trajectories model
XGBoost M3 clinical plus laboratory trajectories plus 20 polygenic risk scores model

links.effect: Bio Me AUROC 0.745; aggregate O/E 0.12 vs. 1.00 in AoU, indicating high predictions.
links.quote: Discrimination transferred to Bio  Me (AUROC 0.745) but predictions were systematically high (aggregate O/E 0.12 vs. 1.00 in AoU), consistent with intercept-shift miscalibration; Bio  Me -fit intercept recalibration restored calibration in African American and Hispanic but not European American participants.

links.effect: M3 AUROC 0.813; ΔAUROC 0.164 vs rFSRP and 0.181 vs PCE; both P < 0.001.
links.quote: In the AoU test partition (n = 6,998; 384 cases), M3 achieved AUROC 0.813 (95% CI, 0.788–0.837), outperforming the Revised Framingham Stroke Risk Profile (ΔAUROC 0.164) and Pooled Cohort Equations (ΔAUROC 0.181; both  P < 0.001).

links.effect: Bio Me-fit recalibration restored calibration in African American and Hispanic but not European American participants.

links.outcome: subgroup performance by cohort and race
links.effect: PRS ΔAUROC + 0.042 (P = 0.003) only in Bio Me Hispanic; no significant gain in five other combinations.
links.quote: PRS contribution was significant only in the Bio  Me Hispanic (ΔAUROC + 0.042;  P = 0.003), with no significant within-stratum gain in five other cohort-by-race combinations.
